overview: CATL is the world's largest manufacturer of lithium-ion batteries, headquartered in Ningde, Fujian Province, China, supplying power batteries for electric vehicles and energy storage system (ESS) batteries to automakers and utilities globally. The company is dual-listed, with A-shares on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (ChiNext, 300750) since 2018 and H-shares on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (3750.HK) since May 2025, and reports its financials in RMB. CATL operates 24 battery factories and six R&D centers worldwide, with a product portfolio spanning LFP, ternary (NMC), sodium-ion and next-generation chemistries, plus battery materials/recycling and emerging applications in battery swapping, electric vessels, low-altitude aviation (eVTOL) and data-center power.

business_model.summary: CATL generates revenue primarily from manufacturing and selling EV power batteries (cells, modules, packs) and ESS batteries (cells, cabinets, containerized systems), supplemented by battery materials/recycling and mineral resources. Revenue is largely transactional/contract-based (volume x price per GWh with OEMs and project developers) rather than subscription-style recurring revenue, though long-term supply agreements and joint ventures with automakers provide multi-year visibility. FY2025 lithium-ion battery sales volume reached 661 GWh (+39% YoY); revenue of RMB423.7bn grew 17% YoY with net profit of RMB72.2bn (+42% YoY).
business_model.customer_type: B2B - global automotive OEMs (VW, BMW, Stellantis, Volvo, Toyota, GAC, Changan, FAW, SAIC, Chery), commercial vehicle manufacturers, utility/grid operators, system integrators, and EPC contractors for energy storage
business_model.geographic_mix: Domestic (China) 69.4% of FY2025 revenue, Overseas 30.6% (and growing; overseas gross margin of 31.4% notably exceeds domestic 24.0%, reflecting pricing power in premium overseas OEM relationships and localized manufacturing)

competitive_position.market_position: Global No.1 in power battery usage volume for nine consecutive years (2017-2025) and global No.1 in ESS battery shipments for five consecutive years (2021-2025). FY2025 global EV battery market share was 39.2% (domestic China 43.4%, overseas 30.0%); H1 FY2026 data shows global share rising further to ~40%. Nearest competitor BYD holds roughly 14% global EV battery share, giving CATL close to 3x the share of its next-largest rival.

moat_factors.description: Largest production capacity in the industry (772 GWh in FY2025, 321 GWh under construction) gives purchasing power over raw materials and manufacturing cost advantages; cell defect rate maintains an order-of-magnitude lead over peers

Broadest chemistry portfolio in the industry (LFP, ternary high-nickel, sodium-ion, condensed-matter, dual-core Freevoy architecture) and fastest iteration cycle (Shenxing, Qilin, Naxtra, TENER product lines); largest R&D spend in the sector (RMB22.1bn in FY2025, >23,000 R&D personnel) and leading patent portfolio
Deep co-development relationships and design-wins with both Chinese and global OEMs (VW, BMW, Stellantis, Toyota) create engineering lock-in over multi-year vehicle platform cycles

Choco-Swap (~2,000 stations) and QIJI Energy Swap (300+ stations) networks, plus JV with Octopus Energy for European truck swapping, create an infrastructure moat that is costly for competitors to replicate
Most WEF 'Lighthouse Factories' in the industry and the sole 'Sustainability Lighthouse'; preferred supplier status in premium BEV segment

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on the Chinese EV market and domestic policy support (subsidies, trade-in schemes) for the bulk of volume
Gross margin has been compressing (26.3% FY2025 to 23.9% H1 FY2026 to 20.7% Q3 FY2026) amid industry overcapacity, aggressive ESS pricing competition, and input cost pass-through lags
Geopolitical target: flagged by the US Department of Defense's 1260H 'Chinese military company' list and subject to UFLPA forced-labor scrutiny, creating overhang on US market access
Overseas expansion still a minority of revenue (30.6%) despite years of investment, meaning most growth remains tied to a maturing, highly competitive domestic market

growth_drivers: Energy storage (ESS) demand is the fastest-growing segment: global ESS shipments +79% in FY2025 and +93% YoY in H1 FY2026, driven by renewables grid integration, utility-scale storage, and new demand from AI data centers

Overseas expansion of manufacturing footprint: Hungary (Debrecen) and Spain (Stellantis JV) plants ramping, Indonesia battery industry chain project, supporting overseas market share gains (30.0% in FY2025, ~33.7% by mid-2026) and higher overseas margins

Next-generation chemistries: sodium-ion (Naxtra) reducing lithium dependency, condensed-matter batteries, Freevoy dual-core/multi-chemistry architecture, and ultra-fast-charging Shenxing platform (up to 15C) sustaining technology leadership and price/performance differentiation
Battery swap ecosystem (Choco-Swap, QIJI Energy Swap) scaling rapidly domestically and now expanding to Europe via the Octopus Energy JV for heavy-truck swapping
Emerging applications: low-altitude eVTOL aircraft (AutoFlight), electric vessels (~900 supported), data-center power solutions - optionality beyond core EV/ESS
H-share listing (May 2025, raised ~HKD41bn) funds the Hungary project and provides an international capital platform to support continued globalization
Secular tailwind: global NEV penetration still rising (China NEV passenger penetration 54-55%, Europe ~29-33%) and power battery usage volume growing double digits annually

business.description: Rapid capacity expansion by domestic and foreign rivals (BYD, EVE Energy, CALB, LG Energy Solution) in a maturing Chinese EV market is compressing pricing and margins across the sector

Consolidated gross margin fell from 26.3% (FY2025) to 23.9% (H1 FY2026) to 20.7% (Q3 FY2026); EV battery margin down to ~20.6% in H1 FY2026 from 22.4% a year earlier, driven by rising non-lithium input costs (copper, electrolyte) passed through with a lag and fixed-price ESS contracts signed before input costs rose

business.risk: Customer concentration and OEM bargaining power
business.description: Large automaker customers (both domestic and global) can negotiate pricing and dual/multi-source their battery supply, limiting CATL's pricing power despite scale
Rapid chemistry innovation cycle (solid-state, sodium-ion, LFP improvements) means CATL must continuously out-invest rivals in R&D or risk losing its performance edge

financial.description: USD and EUR-denominated assets, debts and overseas revenue expose the group to RMB/USD and RMB/EUR fluctuations; partially hedged via natural hedges and derivatives

financial.risk: Rising leverage to fund global capacity build-out
financial.description: Total debt increased to RMB185.9bn by Q3 FY2026 from RMB116.9bn at FY2025 year-end as the company funds Hungary, Spain and Indonesia projects, though asset-liability ratio improved post H-share IPO (61.9% at FY2025 vs 65.2% FY2024)

regulatory.risk: China EV subsidy and policy risk
regulatory.description: Domestic sales volumes are sensitive to trade-in subsidy schemes (2025/2026 auto trade-in policies) and the cancellation of mandatory energy-storage-allocation rules in new energy project approvals

Proposed Franco-German EU battery local-content thresholds for EV subsidy and fleet-emission compliance could affect Chinese-owned cells depending on production location; CATL's Hungary (Debrecen) and existing Germany (Arnstadt) plants partially insulate it versus pure Chinese imports, but thresholds and timing remain unsettled

CATL was added to the US Department of Defense's '1260H' list of Chinese military companies (January 2025) and faces a push by a US House committee for UFLPA forced-labor listing; while not yet a Commerce Entity List or OFAC sanction, this creates overhang on US automaker partnerships (e.g., Ford's Michigan LFP plant licensing deal) and potential future restrictions

regulatory.risk: Import/export rules on recycled battery materials
regulatory.description: New 2025 Chinese customs rules on recycled 'black mass' imports affect the materials/recycling segment's supply chain

macro.risk: Lithium and raw material price volatility
macro.description: Lithium, nickel, cobalt, copper and electrolyte price swings affect procurement costs and margins; pass-through to customers occurs with a lag, creating near-term margin volatility (cited driver of FY2026 margin misses)
A slowdown in global economic growth or EV demand (e.g., reduced subsidies, high interest rates affecting auto financing) would directly reduce power battery volumes
Broad Chinese battery sector overcapacity, flagged repeatedly in company risk disclosures, raises the risk of a prolonged price war across the industry

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global EV battery usage volume grew 31.7% in FY2025 to 1,187 GWh and global ESS battery shipments grew 79% to 550 GWh; growth continued into 2026 (EV battery installations +16.3% YoY in H1 FY2026; ESS shipments +93% YoY in H1 FY2026), with energy storage now the faster-growing of the two segments, increasingly driven by AI data-center power demand alongside renewables integration
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high - power battery demand is tied to global auto sales cycles and government EV subsidy policy; ESS demand is tied to utility capex, grid policy, and renewables build-out, which has its own multi-year investment cycle
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate indirect sensitivity via auto financing/consumer affordability for EVs and via the cost of capital for utility-scale ESS and renewables projects

recent_developments.event: Completed H-share listing on HKEX (Main Board), raising HKD41.0bn (net ~HKD40.6bn) at HKD263.00/share, earmarked primarily (90%) for the Hungary Phase I/II project
Record quarterly deliveries and margins; FY2025 gross margin peaked at 26.3%, net profit +42% YoY to RMB72.2bn, global EV battery market share hit a record 39.2%

Gross margin began compressing - Q2 FY2026 consolidated gross margin of ~23.2%, below consensus (~24.8-25%) and down sequentially from Q1, attributed to rising non-lithium input costs (copper, electrolyte) and fixed-price ESS contracts signed before costs rose

Sodium-ion supply agreements (including a reported 60 GWh deal with Beijing Hithium) and battery-swap vehicle co-development agreement with BAIC Group, signaling commercialization inflection for sodium-ion chemistry

Launched Octopus Energy joint venture to build a heavy-duty-truck battery-swapping network in Europe; domestic Choco-Swap network scaled to ~2,000 stations across 180 cities; overseas EV battery market share rose to ~33.7% (Jan-May 2026) from 30.0% in FY2025

Gross margin fell further to 20.7% (per Q3 FY2026 filing) even as revenue grew 58.6% YoY and net profit grew 14.5% YoY, confirming continued margin pressure from competition and input costs despite strong volume growth

Added to the US Department of Defense's '1260H' list of Chinese military companies; CATL disputes the designation and is seeking removal, while a US House committee has separately pushed for a UFLPA forced-labor listing

EU policy discussions (Franco-German joint position) on local-content thresholds for battery/EV subsidies continue to evolve, with implications for how Chinese-owned European-based cell production (CATL's Hungary and Germany plants) is treated

guidance.as_of: H1 FY2026 Interim Report / Q3 FY2026 Quarterly filing

items.notes: No explicit numeric volume guidance disclosed; 9M FY2026 revenue growth of 56.2% YoY implies continued strong volume growth, consistent with FY2025's 39% YoY volume growth (661 GWh)

items.target: Management and sell-side expect unit profit per Wh to stabilize (Citi flagged ~RMB0.11/Wh) even as % margins compress
items.notes: No formal percentage guidance published; realized margins have stepped down each quarter in 2026 (24.8% implied Q1, 23.2% Q2, 20.7% Q3) versus 26.3% in FY2025, driven by input cost pass-through lags and ESS pricing competition; management's risk disclosures emphasize cost reduction and efficiency measures as the primary offsetting response rather than a specific margin target

items.target: Continued build-out - 772 GWh installed capacity at FY2025 year-end plus 321 GWh under construction, with ongoing investment in Zhongzhou, Jining, Fuding, Liyang, Yibin (domestic) and Hungary, Spain (Stellantis JV), Indonesia (overseas)
items.notes: No single-year capex figure disclosed as formal guidance; H-share IPO proceeds (90% of ~HKD40.6bn net) earmarked specifically for Hungary Phase I/II through 31 December 2030
Cumulative dividends approaching RMB100bn as of the FY2025 letter to shareholders; no indication of a change to payout policy

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Zeng Yuqun's FY2025 shareholder letter emphasized 'all-domain growth' - extending electrification beyond passenger EVs into commercial vehicles, vessels, low-altitude aviation, and data centers - alongside continued technology leadership (Naxtra sodium-ion, Freevoy dual-core, TENER Stack) as the primary strategy for sustaining growth amid intensifying competition. Management's risk disclosures (Potential Risks section, FY2025 annual report) explicitly flag intensified market competition from rapid industry capacity expansion and raw material price/supply volatility as the two most significant operational risks, with R&D investment, cost reduction, and global/overseas expansion cited as the principal mitigants. H1 FY2026 interim report reiterates overseas market share gains and ESS/sodium-ion commercialization as near-term growth priorities.

bull_case: Dominant, growing global market share (~39-40% EV battery, #1 in ESS) nearly 3x the next-largest competitor, with scale, cost and technology advantages that are difficult for rivals to replicate

Energy storage is a secular, fast-growing adjacent market (global ESS shipments +79% FY2025, +93% H1 FY2026) with new AI data-center demand providing an additional growth vector largely uncorrelated with the EV cycle

Overseas expansion (Hungary, Spain, Indonesia plants; HKEX listing capital) is still early, with overseas revenue mix (30.6%) and margins (31.4% vs 24.0% domestic) offering a long runway for mix-driven margin improvement as capacity ramps

Technology leadership across multiple chemistries (LFP, ternary, sodium-ion, condensed-matter, dual-core) and fastest innovation cadence in the industry supports continued design-wins with premium global OEMs (VW, BMW, Stellantis, Toyota)

Strong balance sheet and cash generation (FY2025 operating cash flow RMB133.2bn) support a ~50% dividend payout ratio alongside continued reinvestment, and the H-share listing broadened the investor base and funding access
bear_case: Margin trajectory is deteriorating quarter over quarter in 2026 (26.3% to 23.9% to 20.7% gross margin) as Chinese battery sector overcapacity and aggressive ESS pricing competition intensify, raising the risk this is a structural rather than transitory decline

Heavy reliance on the Chinese domestic market (69% of revenue) for both volume and margin exposes CATL to China EV subsidy policy changes and a crowded, subsidized competitive field (BYD, EVE Energy, CALB, Gotion)

US geopolitical risk is rising: the DoD 1260H designation and potential UFLPA forced-labor listing could curtail US market access and complicate partnerships with US-exposed OEMs, even though CATL is not yet on the Commerce Entity List or OFAC sanctions list

European 'Made in Europe' local-content proposals remain unsettled and could still disadvantage Chinese-owned cell production depending on final thresholds, timing, and how CATL's Hungary/Germany plants are treated

Despite years of investment, overseas revenue remains a minority (30.6%) of the business, meaning CATL's growth and profitability are still disproportionately tied to a maturing, intensely competitive Chinese EV and ESS market
